**Test image:** Dense white/pink cottony mycelium covering stem/crown tissue, with many small round yellowish-white sclerotia (mustard-seed sized, ~1-2mm) scattered throughout.

**Key evidence:**
- **Southern Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*): produces dense white cottony mycelium at crown/stem with characteristic small, round, mustard-seed-sized sclerotia that start white and turn tan. This matches the test image exactly.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: eliminated — its sclerotia are much larger, irregular, and dark/black (rat-dropping shaped), clearly visible in Bugwood_14 and Bugwood_23 references.
- All other classes (bacterial wilts, leaf blights, viruses, molds) were visually distinct — no cottony mycelium + small round sclerotia pattern.

The test image's white mycelium + small round sclerotia combination is the definitive visual signature of Southern Blight.
